title: Autogovernance: attested apply + immutable chronicle for batching/caching auto-tuning
creator: Aisha Nguyen
description: Enable a secure, auditable auto-apply path for batching/cache configuration recommendations that meets enterprise compliance requirements. This ticket defines and implements an 'autogovernance' subsystem: (1) strong RBAC for who/what can propose and apply changes, (2) cryptographic attestation and immutable chronicle records for every change envelope, (3) change-management flows with human-in-loop gating and automated rollback triggers, and (4) SIEM/EDR friendly audit streams and packaged compliance reports. Goal: allow Redwood Optimize to push safe batching/cache tweaks into Dedicated and Private deployments with full forensic trail and ability to revert safely without impacting runtime SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Role-based policies enforced: service principals, engineers, and platform roles mapped to allow/propose/apply/rollback actions
All auto-applies create immutable 'change envelopes' containing diff, who/what/why, attestation signature, canary target and rollback plan
Chronicle persisted to append-only store (write-once semantics) and exported to SIEM via structured JSON with configurable retention
Automated pre-apply checks: compatibility matrix, quantization profile match, throughput/liveness dry-run, and safety budget thresholds
Canary window and metrics-based criteria defined; failure during canary triggers automatic rollback and alerting
Operators can perform manual abort/force-apply only with recorded justification and 2-step approval for high-risk changes
Audit UI in Console surfaces change timeline, attestation chain, and raw artifacts; downloadable compliance report for SOC/ISO assessments
technical_notes: RBAC model: extend our IAM to include 'autotuner:propose', 'autotuner:apply', 'autotuner:rollback' actions. Map to SSO groups + service accounts.
Attestation: sign change envelope with KMS-backed key; include nonce, timestamp, git commit of policy-as-code, and runtime fingerprint.
Chronicle store: use append-only ledger backed by object-store + manifest index. Ensure immutability via KMS-signed manifests and object-store versioning.
Policy engine: run pre-apply Rego policies (OPA) that check for latency regressions, memory/kv cache footprint, and quantization compatibility.
Canary runtime: support fractional routing to canary pool; metrics sampled at 1s granularity for first 5m then 10s for next 25m; rollback on >3 SD degradation or error rate delta >0.5%.
Rollback harness: automated snapshot of config and KV cache pointers; plan to restore last known-good manifest and a 'throttle warmup' to avoid thundering restarts.
Observability: wire events to Console timeline, create structured events to /events/audit with schema versioned; add a compliance export endpoint for audit retention windows.
Secrets: short-lived signed tokens for auto-apply runner; operators cannot extract long-term credentials.
Compliance: provide canned report template (SOC2/ISO) that references chronicle hashes, KMS key ids, and approval records.
Performance safety: dry-run with shadow traffic for heavy-batching changes to ensure latency SLO remains within 10% for the slowest p50/p95 buckets before applying to production.
Failure modes: define soft-failure (revert to previous config with no service disruption) and hard-failure (fallback to lower-perf model variant) playbooks.
